analysis: Only base-side text for ClusterService.swift (lines 1-911) was supplied, plus a truncated patch excerpt. The visible patch adds a private `environment: [String: String]?` property and an init parameter (default nil, meaning the process's own environment at each start), documented as "the environment this Mac's parts start from (`partEnvironment`)". It is internal, not public, and the public convenience init is unchanged. The other hunks (head ~1131, 1301, 1428, 1448-1463) are not visible. They likely include the `partEnvironment` implementation and the use of it where parts are spawned, plus changes to approval handling around `serveLocally`, but I could not verify any of this. The base code I examined (control.lock flock, service.lock, 0600 files, private directories, SIGTERM-only stop with start-time-checked PIDs, local API token sent only to our own solo server, pairing-gated link commands with claim/supersede checks, followsPeer checks) shows no visible regression from the visible patch. Open questions for integration: (1) how `partEnvironment` merges or filters the environment passed to child parts. If it forwards the service's environment, or an injected one, including DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE or other security-relevant variables such as cache-kill, TTL or disk settings (T-041) or provider tokens (A-008), the question is whether any secret or policy toggle crosses a trust boundary. (2) The hidden approval-hunk change at head ~1131. It touches `serveLocally` and approvalNote and could affect which approval state governs serving (T-052/T-053 territory, TB-011). Both depend on code not provided, so this is a coverage limit, not evidence of safety.
